game.title: Read the Graph: Data Literacy Essentials
game.description: A data-literacy check for intro statistics or any class that reads charts: center and spread, variable types, correlation, skew, outliers and misleading axes. Every chart uses made-up example data.

images.description: Scatter plot of 30 points rising from lower left to upper right in a tight band
Scatter plot of 30 points spread out with no visible trend
Scatter plot of 30 points falling from upper left to lower right in a tight band
Scatter plot of 30 points drifting loosely downward from left to right, widely scattered
Histogram of minutes waited at a campus help desk by 200 visitors, in 5-minute bins from 0 to 60. Most bars are on the left, with a long tail to the right.
Bar chart of units sold. Product A is 52 and Product B is 56; the vertical axis starts at 50 and runs to 57.
Scatter plot of exam score against hours studied for 37 students; scores generally rise with hours studied.

questions.prompt: Warm-up: where do you run into charts and graphs most often?
What is the median of this data set? 4, 9, 2, 7, 15
Which of these are measures of spread (variability)? Select all that apply.
Sort each variable: is it categorical or quantitative?
Which scatter plot shows the strongest negative correlation?
True or false: for the data in this right-skewed histogram, the mean wait time is greater than the median wait time.
True or false: a correlation of r = −0.8 shows a weaker linear relationship than r = 0.5.
This chart's vertical axis starts at 50, so bar B looks three times as tall as bar A. What is the actual percentage increase from A (52) to B (56)?
Find the outlier: pick the cell with the one student whose score breaks the trend.
The value that appears most often in a data set is called the ___.
Exit ticket: which topics should we review next class? Select all that apply.
